To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the softening of the hadronic equation of state is due to the restoration of chiral symmetry, while the softening of a mixed phase equation of state is mainly due to the presence two conserved charges.

the equation of state at high temperatures and densities can be softened by chiral symmetry restoration and/or by the formation of clusters, and that the bulk modulus is strongly dependent on temperature and on the nature of the new degrees of freedom.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two different scenarios for the softening of the EOS.

the study of the equation of states of dense matter in the presence of new degrees of freedoms, and in particular, we have investigated the effect of a softening of this equation of state on the properties of neutron stars.
the study of a possible softening of the EOS in the hadronic phase due to chiral restoration and in the mixed-phase due to the formation of clusters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a softening of a hadronic equation of state at high densities and temperatures may be due to chiral restoration and/or quark decon-finement, but the two phenomena are different and their effects on the equation of state are not equivalent.
the mixed phase is softer than the hadronic matter, while the hadronic phase is softer than quark matter.
, at high densities and temperatures, a phase transition to the deconfined phase is not a necessary condition to produce a softening of matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the softening of the EOS due to chiral restoration is a more natural scenario for neutron stars than the softening due to the appearance in the mixed phase.

the bulk modulus in a hadron gas is mainly dependent on density, while in a mixed phase the bulk modulus is strongly dependent on temperature and it does not vanish due to the presence the two conserved charges.

the softening of the hadronic equation of state due to chiral-sym-metry restoration is a much more natural mechanism to explain the softening of nuclear matter than the mixed-phase model, which has been used to describe the softening of matter in neutron stars and in the quark-gluon plasma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the softening of the EOS is not a sufficient condition to obtain the existence of a first-order transition in the mixed-phase region.
the softening of the EOS due to chiral restoration is more relevant for the study of neutron star properties than the softening due to quark decon-finement.
the softening of the EOS is not necessarily due to the formation of a deconfined quark-gluon phase.
